evidence_quotes: Tobelo, Indonesia led all hotspots with 19 earthquakes — nearly one every two days — making it the single most active zone
Mohr, Iran registered 15 events, including a shallow M4.9 (8.5 km deep) on February 12
The Aleutian/Nikolski corridor in Alaska saw 13 events
persistent shallow events (some under 10 km deep) can cause disproportionate surface damage even at moderate magnitudes
this subduction zone is capable of generating large tsunamis with little warning should a major rupture occur
criticisms: No concrete recommended actions are provided — the report never tells a coordinator to 'alert county X', 'pre-position resources at Y', 'request a USGS update on Z', or 'verify shelter capacity in W'. The Risk Watch section describes risk but stops short of prescribing any action.

Monitoring priorities are vague: 'close monitoring' and 'deserve close monitoring' are not actionable watch items. The report does not specify which magnitude bands to watch, what thresholds should trigger escalation, or which specific agencies or partners to notify.
No 'next 7 days' forward-looking operational window is defined — a coordinator cannot tell from this report when to stand down or escalate.

The Data Caveat explicitly states the report 'should not be used for real-world emergency planning or public safety decisions,' which directly undermines any operational utility the report might otherwise have.

Prioritization is partially visible (Tobelo ranked first, Mohr second, Alaska third) but no explicit 'highest-risk' framing or tiered action levels (e.g., Watch vs. Advisory vs. Information) are assigned to distinguish response urgency.
